title: Foundation
copy: The National Resistance Movement takes power in a country exhausted by conflict. The work begins with the hardest material there is: trust.

milestones.text: A fundamental change — the rebuilding of the nation begins.
Currency reform and an IMF-backed recovery programme begin to tame hyperinflation.

title: Stabilisation
copy: A new constitution, the first direct presidential election, and a public-health campaign the world would study. The state finds its footing.

milestones.text: A new national constitution resets the legal foundation.
The first directly elected president in Uganda's history takes office.
Universal Primary Education opens the school gates to millions.
National HIV prevalence falls by around seventy percent — a global model.

title: Growth
copy: The economy compounds. Farms feed factories; enrolment climbs; a landmark refugee law opens the national door and keeps it open.

milestones.text: A landmark Refugee Act — among the world's most progressive — is enacted.
Vision 2040, the long-term blueprint for a modern nation, is approved.

title: Transformation
copy: Power on the Nile. Expressways, bridges and transmission lines carry the decade; the grid reaches districts that had never been connected.

milestones.text: The Isimba Dam and the Kampala–Entebbe Expressway come online.

title: Acceleration
copy: Karuma lifts national capacity past two thousand megawatts. Industry deepens, and the first barrels of commercial oil come into view.

milestones.text: The 600 MW Karuma Dam lifts national capacity past 2,000 MW.
Forty years of nation-building — as commercial oil production begins.

title: The Next Horizon
copy: The record does not close; it compounds. The next chapter is capacity — industrial, human, and institutional.

milestones.text: Vision 2040: a transformed Ugandan society — from a peasant to a modern and prosperous country.
